items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: One week after the visit of "Wild Bill" and his friend, they came back to Woodlawn Inn and Bill wanted to play my horn again

ctx.x: At that time, even though he was two years younger than I was, he was blowing a whole lot more trumpet than me. I was able to read fairly well, but I was not too well educated in different keys. My range was not more than high 'C'. Probably I could have changed that by using different mouth pieces but I didn't get to know about things like that until I met Louis Armstrong later on. Even so, high notes never really bothered me, I had a good enough range for the time although I was not as gifted as players like…

One week after the visit of "Wild Bill" and his friend, they came back to Woodlawn Inn and Bill wanted to play my horn again, but he was so drunk that he could hardly stand. I let him blow my horn but he really didn't play anything that night and I had my revenge because I blew him out. His friend came to get him and put him in a back room where he immediately went to sleep.

Then this friend of Bill's came back to talk with us and it was then that he noticed the playing of Edgar Hayes and it hit him like a man being hit on his head with a blackjack. He asked Edgar to play some numbers that we didn't know and after two or three numbers almost everyone at the Inn that night was standing around the bandstand listening to the pianist.
